# Grok Build session fixtures

These reduced files target **Grok Build 1.0.52**, checked locally in a scratch `GROK_HOME`. They keep the fields cornercase reads and drop everything else. Paths are `/home/user/...`. Session ids, account ids and request ids are replaced. `summary.json` has no `agent_id` and no `attempt_id`. Nothing here is a credential, and cornercase never reads `auth.json`.

A pane is the row in `active_sessions.json` whose `pid` is the foreground process. On Linux that row's `pid_start` has to match field 22 of `/proc/<pid>/stat` (clock ticks since boot). A missing start time, which is what macOS returns, does not reject the row. The session directory is `sessions/<percent-encoded cwd>/<id>/`, with uppercase hex and the RFC 3986 unreserved characters left as they are. When that name would be longer than a file name, Grok writes a short directory plus a sibling `.cwd` file holding the path; cornercase finds the id and checks `.cwd` or `summary.json`'s `info.cwd` instead of rebuilding the hash.

`events.jsonl` `turn_ended` ends a turn (`completed` or `cancelled`). `turn_completed` in `updates.jsonl` is the usage record, not the end of the turn. The reader keeps a tail and the fold across polls, and on the first read (or when the file is replaced) seeds an open turn from the newest `turn_started` or `turn_ended` behind that tail. If the backwards scan reaches its bound without either marker, newer phase or tool events keep the turn working until `turn_ended`. Waiting is a `permission_prompt` phase, a `permission_requested` that has no later `permission_resolved` for the same tool, or an open `ask_user_question` or `exit_plan_mode` until `tool_completed`. A live plan approval was `exit_plan_mode`: its permission returned `allow` with `wait_ms` 0 while the ask stayed open, and `tool_completed` came when it was approved, after which the turn continued. `enter_plan_mode` is entering plan mode, kept in its own fixtures. Resolving one permission leaves another request waiting. Other tools stay working. `waiting_for_model` is the normal start of a turn. An unknown model is rejected before any turn; a `turn_started` with no `turn_ended` in real logs is not explained yet, and there is no timeout. A title containing `Action Required` means waiting only while the turn is open. A braille spinner, and the word Waiting in a compact title, do not.

Ctrl+C ends the turn (`cancelled`, `mid_turn_abort`, `cancellation_context.trigger` `ctrl_c`). One Enter while a turn is open queues the text. A second Enter sends it now: the open turn is `cancelled` with trigger `send_now`, and the next `turn_started` has `redirect_kind` `queued_after_cancel`. `send` presses Enter once, so it queues.

The context percentage is the newest primary one-call `turn_completed` when it matches the model and is newer than compaction and newer than a recorded `turn_started` for the new model. A model change that is only in `summary.json` drops that reply and the current `signals.json` reading until a newer reply or a newer signals file. A multi-call turn uses `signals.json` `contextTokensUsed` over `contextWindowTokens` when the file is at least as new as that reply, `primaryModelId` matches, and nothing newer invalidates it. `contextWindowUsage`, `compactionCount` and `_meta.totalTokens` are not the figure. Stats take `inputTokens - cachedReadTokens`, `outputTokens`, `cachedReadTokens` and `cacheCreationTokens`, and do not add `reasoningTokens` again.

A prompt is a `user_message_chunk` with `promptIndex`. `syntheticPrompt` true is never a prompt and false always is, even when the text begins with `<system-reminder>` or `<user_info>`; that tag check is only for a chunk that omits the field. Its time is `agentTimestampMs`. One submission is that index plus the millisecond. A monitor event (`syntheticPrompt`, often a `<monitor-event>`) is not a prompt. `chat_history.jsonl` is not used to pair prompts. A prompt belongs to the turn interval that covers its time. A `turn_completed` belongs to the newest turn that started at or before it, including a few milliseconds after `turn_ended`, and a worker completion adds tokens only. A separate subagent directory was not captured.

The last message is the newest assistant string in `chat_history.jsonl`. Its time is the `agent_message_chunk` whose text is that string, not a later `turn_ended`. `trust.txt` is the folder question (`Yes, proceed`), which the default trust pattern matches. `active_sessions.json` is one pane row.

`/` and `!` are local commands. `?` is a real prompt. There is no plan-usage probe. Resume is `grok <args> --resume <summary info.id>`.
